newsitem.title: GERMANY: Foreign sales boost Audi first half.
newsitem.headline: Foreign sales boost Audi first half.

text.p: Audi AG said Friday that group pre-tax profit climbed 21 percent in the first half of this year to 489 million marks ($262.2 million), driven by strong foreign demand for its luxury cars.

Audi, the luxury arm of Volkswagen AG, said group sales increased 13.7 percent during the half to 10.6 billion marks ($5.7 billion) -- an increase that analysts said came largely from its mainstay A4 sedan.

Audi said deliveries during the fist half climbed 12.6 percent to 276,052, on pace for a company target this year of at least 500,000 deliveries. German deliveries climbed 10.5 percent to 121,835 units.
Audi also was doing well in the United States, the world's largest car market and an area of difficulty for the company until the last year or two.
Audi had previously reported it sold 17,019 new vehicles in the United States, an increase of 34 percent and its best performance there in 10 years.
